title: Nvidia CEO on AI Market Turmoil: ‘All of This Is Going to Pass’
source_used: Bloomberg, as relayed by The Straits Times (Bloomberg page returned HTTP 403)
key_facts: Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang spoke to Bloomberg's Emily Chang at an event in Berlin.
He said the AI sell-off will pass because AI will be transformative for every industry and country.
He called recent news 'choppy' and said it will not change the fundamentals; he urged investors to stay focused on first principles.
The Philadelphia Stock Exchange Semiconductor Index has fallen eight straight days, the longest losing streak since 2008.
Nvidia shares dropped in seven of the past eight sessions; investors worry AI spending is not sustainable at a time of higher borrowing costs.
CoreWeave, a cloud-computing provider that counts Nvidia as one of its biggest backers, saw its bonds hit levels that typically signal distress and its stock lose a quarter of its value this week.
quote_evidence: “All of this is going to pass, and the reason for that is very simple,” Huang told Bloomberg’s Emily Chang during an event in Berlin.
The closely watched Philadelphia Stock Exchange Semiconductor Index has now fallen for eight straight days, marking the longest losing streak since 2008.
The company’s bonds recently hit levels that typically signal distress, and the stock lost a quarter of its value this week.
why_it_matters_hint: The head of the biggest AI chip seller tells jittery investors the sell-off will pass, while chip shares post their longest losing streak since 2008.
event_date: 16 Oct 2026 (Bloomberg's article date; the day of the interview is not stated)
notes: Bloomberg page blocked (HTTP 403, robot check); text read in The Straits Times, which publishes the Bloomberg article (credited 'BLOOMBERG' at its end). Huang's view is a prediction by the head of the company that sells the chips.
